theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What does "professionalism" at work mean?
options: Wearing expensive clothes and jewellery to work each and every day
Behaving in a skilled, reliable and respectful way at work
Doing only the work that is written in your contract
Having worked in the same trade for more than ten years

questions.stem: What is "ethics" at work?
options: The rules for how much each worker is paid
The list of tools that the business owns
Knowing and doing what is right and fair
The times when the workplace opens and closes

questions.stem: Your shift starts at 8:00 a.m. When should you arrive?
options: At 8:00 a.m. exactly, then change and get ready
Any time before 9:00 a.m., as long as you stay late to make up
At 8:15 a.m., because the first job is never urgent
A few minutes early, so that you are ready to start at 8:00

questions.stem: You will be late because the bus has broken down. What should you do?
options: Call your supervisor before the shift starts and explain
Say nothing and explain when you get there
Stay home for the whole day, because you will be late anyway
Ask a co-worker to sign you in on time

questions.stem: Why should workers follow the dress code, such as a clean uniform or overalls?
options: So that they look the same as the workers at other firms
Because clean clothes make the work go much faster
It shows respect, looks professional and can protect them
So that the customer will not ask them any questions

questions.stem: Why is personal hygiene especially important for a beauty therapist or a hotel worker?
options: They work close to clients, and germs can spread
It is the only rule that they need to follow at work
It allows them to charge higher prices for services
Clients never notice it, so it does not matter much

questions.stem: A customer pays you $500 too much by mistake. What should you do?
options: Keep it as a tip without saying anything
Tell the customer and give the money back
Put it in the cash box and tell nobody about it
Share it with the co-worker who saw it

questions.stem: Which of these is a form of stealing time from an employer?
options: Taking the lunch break that your contract allows you
Asking a supervisor how to do a task
Finishing a job before the deadline
Long personal phone calls during work hours

questions.stem: Is it all right to take offcuts of steel, spare cable or salon products home without asking?
options: Yes, because the business will only throw them away in the end
Yes, if the amount is small and nobody will miss it
Yes, as long as you only use them for your own family
No, they belong to the business unless you have permission

questions.stem: A client tells you about a health problem during a treatment. What should you do with this information?
options: Tell your co-workers so that they can be kind to her
Keep it private and use it only to serve her safely
Post about it online without using her name
Tell her friends so that they can help her

questions.stem: What should you do if a customer asks for work you are not trained or qualified to do?
options: Explain politely and refer it to a qualified person
Try it anyway so that the customer is not let down
Do the job and charge less in case it goes wrong
Watch an online video quickly and then do the job

questions.stem: An electrical trainee is asked by a neighbour to rewire a house alone, for cash. What is the professional response?
options: Do it at night so that nobody finds out about it
Do it, but charge a low price as a trainee
Refuse, and say the work needs a qualified electrician
Do it quickly, and leave out the parts you are unsure of

questions.stem: A supplier offers you a gift to choose their products for your workplace. What should you do?
options: Refuse it or report it to your supervisor, as the rules say
Accept it quietly and then choose their products as asked
Accept it and ask for a bigger gift next time
Accept it, then share it out fairly among all your co-workers

questions.stem: What is a "conflict of interest" at work?
options: When two workers argue about who should clean up
When a customer complains about the price of a job
When the business has far too many jobs to finish on time this week
When your own gain could affect a decision you make for work

questions.stem: What does it mean to be "accountable" for your work?
options: Being the person who counts the money at the end of the day
Keeping a list of the hours your co-workers have worked
Accepting responsibility for your work and its results
Blaming others when something you did goes wrong

questions.stem: You notice that a weld you made yesterday on a customer's gate has a crack. What should you do?
options: Paint over the crack so that the customer does not see it
Tell your supervisor and arrange for it to be repaired
Say nothing, because the gate has already been fitted
Blame the crack on the steel from the supplier

questions.stem: Why must workers follow the workplace's policies and procedures?
options: So that the supervisor has more forms to sign each day
To keep work safe, fair and done to the same standard
Because policies are only for new workers to read
So that workers never have to think for themselves

questions.stem: What is a "code of conduct"?
options: A written set of rules for how staff should behave
A secret password used to open the workshop door
A list of prices that the business charges
The number printed on each worker's ID card

questions.stem: You see a co-worker stealing materials from the stores. What should you do?
options: Ignore it, because it is not your business
Ask the co-worker to share some with you
Tell the customers about it when they come in
Report it to your supervisor or manager

questions.stem: When is it acceptable to use your personal phone for social media at work?
options: Any time, as long as the customer does not notice
While using a grinder or other machine
During breaks, away from customers and work areas
While a client is sitting and waiting for her treatment

questions.stem: Why must a worker never come to work under the influence of alcohol or drugs?
options: Because it always makes the worker arrive far too early in the day
Because the uniform will not fit properly
It slows reactions and judgement and can cause accidents
Because customers prefer workers who are tired

questions.stem: Which pricing practice is ethical?
options: Charging tourists a higher price without telling them
Adding work to the bill that was never actually done for them
Using cheap parts but charging for good ones
Giving a clear price and explaining any extra costs first

questions.stem: A customer is in a hurry. What should a professional do about the quality of the work?
options: Skip all of the checks so that the customer can leave sooner
Keep to the quality standard and agree a fair time
Do only half the job and charge the full price
Rush the job and leave the clean-up for later

questions.stem: Why should a tradesperson keep learning new skills after getting qualified?
options: Methods, tools and rules change over time
So that they never have to work again
Because a certificate runs out after one week
So that they can stop following safety rules

questions.stem: Which shows respect for a customer's property, such as their home or car?
options: Covering and protecting it and cleaning up after the job
Leaving rubbish there for the customer to deal with
Using the customer's own tools and things without asking first
Moving their things around without saying anything

questions.stem: What is the ethical way to get rid of used chemicals, oil or old electrical parts?
options: Pour them into the nearest drain or gully when nobody is looking
Burn them in the yard behind the workshop
Follow the maker's and the Centre's disposal rules
Throw them in the bush behind the building

questions.stem: A co-worker asks you to sign the attendance sheet for them because they will be late. What should you do?
options: Sign it, because they would do the same for you
Sign it only if they pay you for doing it
Sign it, but only this one time
Refuse politely, because it would be dishonest

questions.stem: Which information should you keep confidential?
options: The opening hours shown on the shop sign
Customers' phone numbers, addresses and bills
The name of the business painted on the front gate
The public prices on the board outside

questions.stem: A customer was rude to you today. What is the professional thing to do on social media?
options: Post the customer's name and photo to warn others
Write a long post about how bad the customer was
Ask your friends to send rude messages to them
Post nothing about it, and report it at work

questions.stem: What is a strong "work ethic"?
options: Working hard and doing a good job without being watched
Working only when the supervisor is in the room
Knowing a great deal about the ethics of other businesses
Working very fast, even if the quality is poor

questions.stem: You think a workplace rule is unfair. What is the professional way to deal with it?
options: Break the rule until it is changed
Complain about it to the customers
Raise it politely with your supervisor
Tell all the new trainees that they can ignore the rule

questions.stem: Which is professional behaviour towards customers?
options: Serving friends first, even if others came before them
Treating every customer fairly and with respect
Giving better service to customers who look rich
Ignoring customers who do not speak clearly

questions.stem: A supervisor asks you to use a grinder with a cracked disc to finish a job quickly. What should you do?
options: Use it, but stand a little further back
Refuse to use it, explain why, and ask for a new disc
Use it, because the supervisor is the one who gave the order
Use it only for the last few cuts of the job

questions.stem: Why do some trades, such as electrical work, require a licence or certificate before you can work alone?
options: So that the government can collect more money from workers
So that only older people can work in the trade
So that workers can charge any price they like
To show the worker is trained to do the work safely

questions.stem: How should you speak to a client while you work?
options: Politely, using their name and suitable language
Using slang and jokes that only your friends get
Loudly, so that the whole salon or shop can hear
About your own personal problems at home

questions.stem: You promised a customer that their job would be ready on Friday, but it will be late. What should you do?
options: Say nothing and hope the customer does not come
Tell the customer that it is ready, then rush to get it finished
Contact the customer early, explain and give a new date
Blame the delay on a co-worker who was off sick

questions.stem: Why can a worker's behaviour outside work, such as in uniform in public, affect the business?
options: It cannot, because work and home are always separate
Only the owner's behaviour ever affects the business
People link what they see to the business's good name
Because uniforms can only be worn inside the workplace

questions.stem: You were 30 minutes late today. What should you write on your time sheet?
options: Your usual start time, as you will work faster
The real time you started work
No time at all, so nobody can check it
The time your co-worker started

questions.stem: What does "integrity" mean?
options: Being honest and doing right even when no one is watching
Being the best-paid and most senior worker in the whole business
Finishing every job faster than anyone else
Always agreeing with whatever the supervisor says

questions.stem: A customer asks for your opinion of a competitor's work. What is the professional reply?
options: Say that the competitor is dishonest and lazy
Tell untrue stories so that the customer stays with you
Laugh and say that their work always falls apart
Speak about your own work and avoid running others down

questions.stem: A customer complains about your work. What is the professional first step?
options: Tell the customer that they are wrong
Ask the customer to leave the premises
Refuse to talk about it at all until some time tomorrow
Listen calmly and find out the full problem

questions.stem: You have a fever and a bad cough on a work day. What is the professional thing to do?
options: Go in and work closely with clients as usual
Go in to work, but do not tell anyone that you are ill at all
Tell your supervisor and follow the sick-leave rules
Stay home without telling anyone at work

questions.stem: Is it right to use the workplace's machines or vehicle for your own private jobs?
options: Yes, if you do it after working hours
Only with permission from the owner or manager
Yes, as long as nobody sees you do it
Yes, because you already use them every single day at work

questions.stem: Why must test results and job records, such as an electrical test sheet, be filled in truthfully?
options: Others rely on them to know the work is safe
So that the records look tidy in the file
Because nobody else will ever read them
So that the job seems to take longer than it did

questions.stem: Which list best describes a professional worker?
options: Punctual, honest, skilled, polite and safe
Fast, loud, careless, cheap and late
Rich, famous, well dressed, strong and popular
Quiet, lazy, rude, untidy and absent

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What one word means arriving on time and keeping to agreed times?
What is the word for money or a gift offered to make someone act dishonestly, for example to win a contract?
What do we call a worker who reports wrongdoing at their workplace to someone who can act on it?
What is the name for the rules on what staff must wear at work?
What word means keeping your body and clothes clean so that germs do not spread?
At work, who is usually the first person you should report unsafe or dishonest behaviour to?
What is the name of the document an employer and a worker sign that sets out the job, the pay and the hours?
What word names the good or bad name that a worker or a business has with the public?
What is the word for staying away from work often, without a good reason?
What do the letters "CPD" stand for, meaning ongoing learning after you qualify?
What word means being polite and showing good manners to customers?
What document does a customer receive to prove that they have paid?
What is the name of the document that shows you have passed a course or are qualified in a trade?
What word means treating everyone equally and without favourites?
Your shift starts at 8:00 a.m. and your supervisor asks you to arrive 10 minutes early. What time should you arrive?

essays.stem: Explain what professionalism means at work, and describe five ways a worker can show it.
essays.modelAnswer: Professionalism means behaving at work in a skilled, reliable, honest and respectful way, so that customers and employers can trust you. First, a professional is punctual: they arrive on time, ready to work, and give notice if they will be late or absent. Second, they look the part: a clean uniform or overalls, good personal hygiene and the correct PPE. Third, they are honest: they charge fairly, record their hours truthfully and do not take what is not theirs. Fourth, they treat customers and co-workers with respect, speak politely and keep private information confidential. Fifth, they take pride in the quality of their work, follow the workplace's procedures and safety rules, own up to mistakes and put them right. A professional also keeps learning, to stay up to date with new methods and tools.
markingPoints: Defines professionalism (skilled, reliable, honest, respectful)
Punctuality and attendance
Appearance, hygiene and PPE
Honesty and respect, including confidentiality
Quality work, following procedures, owning mistakes or keeping learning

essays.stem: Explain why honesty and integrity matter in your trade. Give examples of honest and dishonest behaviour.
essays.modelAnswer: Honesty means telling the truth and not stealing or cheating. Integrity means doing what is right even when no one is watching. They matter because customers must trust a tradesperson in their homes, with their money and with their safety. An employer must trust workers with tools, materials and cash. A worker who is caught being dishonest can lose the job, the business loses customers, and the worker's name is spoiled in the community. Examples of honest behaviour are giving back money paid by mistake, charging only for work done, using the materials the customer paid for, and filling in time sheets and test records truthfully. Examples of dishonest behaviour are taking offcuts or products home without permission, adding extra hours to a bill, using cheap parts while charging for good ones, or signing in for a late co-worker.
markingPoints: Explains honesty and integrity
Customers and employers must be able to trust the worker
Results of dishonesty (job loss, lost customers, bad name)
At least two examples of honest behaviour
At least two examples of dishonest behaviour

essays.stem: Describe what you should do if you see a co-worker doing something dishonest, such as stealing materials or cheating a customer.
essays.modelAnswer: I should not join in, accept a share, or pretend I did not see it, because that would make me part of the wrongdoing. I should not argue with or threaten the co-worker in public, because that can lead to a fight and does not solve the problem. I would write down what I saw, the date, the time and the place, as soon as I can, while I still remember the details. Then I would report it privately to my supervisor or, if the supervisor is involved, to the manager or owner, following the workplace's rules for reporting. I would tell only the facts, not rumours. I would keep the matter confidential and not gossip about it with other workers. The business can then look into it fairly and protect its customers and property.
markingPoints: Does not join in, accept a share or ignore it
Does not confront in public or threaten
Records the facts: what, when, where
Reports privately to the supervisor or a manager, as the rules say
Keeps it confidential and sticks to facts

essays.stem: Explain why confidentiality is important when dealing with customers, and describe how a worker keeps information confidential.
essays.modelAnswer: Customers often share private information with a worker: their address, phone number, what they paid, when their house is empty, or a health problem that affects a treatment. If this information is passed on, the customer could be embarrassed, cheated or even robbed, and they would lose trust in the business. The business could also lose customers and face legal trouble. A worker keeps information confidential by sharing it only with staff who need it to do the job. They do not talk about customers to friends or family, and they never post about customers or their homes on social media. They keep job cards, client record cards and receipts in a safe place, not left lying around. They do not read out private details where others can hear, and they lock phones and computers that hold customer information.
markingPoints: Gives examples of private customer information
Harm if it is shared: embarrassment, theft, loss of trust
Shares only with staff who need it
Does not discuss customers or post about them on social media
Stores records safely and protects phones or computers

essays.stem: Explain why a worker should only do work they are trained and qualified to do. Give examples from at least two trades.
essays.modelAnswer: A worker who does a job they are not trained for may do it wrongly. This can injure the worker or the customer, damage property and cost money to put right. It can also break the law or the rules of the trade, and the business's insurance may not cover the damage. The professional way is to explain politely that the job is outside what you are trained to do, and to refer the customer to a qualified person or ask your supervisor. For example, an electrical trainee should not rewire a house alone, because a mistake could cause a shock or a fire. A beauty therapist should not treat a skin infection or a strange mole, but should advise the client to see a doctor. A welding trainee should not weld a gas cylinder or a fuel tank, which needs special training and procedures.
markingPoints: Risk of injury, damage and cost
May break rules or the law; insurance may not cover it
Explain politely and refer to a qualified person or supervisor
Correct example from one trade
Correct example from a second trade

essays.stem: Describe the personal appearance and hygiene expected of a professional worker, and explain why each part matters.
essays.modelAnswer: A professional worker bathes daily and uses deodorant, because they work close to customers and co-workers and body odour gives a poor impression. Their uniform, overalls or apron should be clean and in good repair, as the dress code says, because it shows respect and helps customers trust the business. Hair should be neat and, where needed, tied back or covered, so that it cannot be caught in a machine or fall onto a client. Nails should be short and clean, especially in beauty and food work, to stop germs spreading. Jewellery should be kept to a minimum, because rings and chains can catch on tools or conduct electricity. The correct PPE, such as safety boots, gloves or a face mask, must be worn and kept clean. Hands should be washed before and after each client or job.
markingPoints: Daily bathing and fresh breath or deodorant, with a reason
Clean uniform as the dress code says, with a reason
Hair neat and tied back; nails clean and short, with reasons
Little or no jewellery, with a safety reason
Correct PPE and hand washing

essays.stem: While your boss is away, a customer offers you cash to do a private job for them using the business's tools and materials. Explain what you would do and why.
essays.modelAnswer: I would politely refuse the offer. I would explain that the tools and materials belong to the business and I am not allowed to use them for private work. Taking the job would be dishonest, because I would be using my employer's property and time to make money for myself. It would also be a conflict of interest, because I would be taking business away from my employer. If anything went wrong with the job, the customer would have no guarantee and the business's insurance would not cover it. I would offer to book the job properly through the business and take the customer's details so that my boss can call them with a price. When my boss returns, I would tell them about the request. This keeps my job, my honesty and the trust of my employer.
markingPoints: Refuses politely
Explains the tools and materials belong to the business
Says it is dishonest or a conflict of interest
Offers to book the job properly through the business
Tells the boss about the request

essays.stem: Explain how a worker should deal with a mistake they have made on a customer's job.
essays.modelAnswer: First, the worker should stop and check how serious the mistake is, especially if it could make the job unsafe, such as a cracked weld, a loose electrical connection or a chemical left on a client's skin too long. If there is any danger, they must make it safe at once. Next, they should tell their supervisor honestly what happened, without hiding it or blaming someone else. With the supervisor, they should tell the customer, say sorry, and explain what will be done to put it right and when. Then they should fix the mistake properly, at no extra cost to the customer if the fault was theirs. Finally, they should think about why it happened and what they will do differently, so that it does not happen again, and record it if the workplace requires.
markingPoints: Checks the mistake and makes it safe at once if there is danger
Tells the supervisor honestly; does not hide it or blame others
Tells the customer, says sorry and explains the fix
Puts it right properly
Learns from it so that it does not happen again

essays.stem: Describe how a worker can keep improving their skills and professional standards during their career.
essays.modelAnswer: A worker can take short courses and higher-level qualifications, for example moving from Level 2 to Level 3 in their trade. They can attend workshops and demonstrations from suppliers to learn about new tools, machines and products. They can read the maker's instructions and safety data for new products and equipment. They can learn from experienced co-workers by watching, asking questions and asking for feedback on their own work. They can keep up with changes in safety rules and the standards their trade must meet. They can join a trade association or group to meet others and share good practice. They can also set personal goals each year and keep a record of training they have done. Learning in this way helps them work more safely, do better quality work and earn more.
markingPoints: Further courses and qualifications
Supplier demonstrations and reading the maker's instructions
Learning from experienced workers and asking for feedback
Keeping up with safety rules and standards, or joining a trade group
Setting goals and recording training; benefits to the worker

essays.stem: Explain how poor attendance and lateness affect the team, the customers and the business.
essays.modelAnswer: When a worker is late or absent, the rest of the team must cover their work. This means more pressure and longer hours for others, which can lead to tiredness, mistakes and bad feeling in the team. A team task, such as lifting a heavy gate or a salon fully booked with clients, may have to stop or be done with too few people, which can also be unsafe. Customers are affected because jobs start late, appointments are moved or cancelled, and promises are broken, so they may go to a competitor. The business loses money because work is not finished, it may have to pay overtime, and its reputation suffers. Good attendance and punctuality show that a worker can be trusted and are often a reason for promotion.
markingPoints: Team: extra work and pressure for others
Team: bad feeling or unsafe short-handed work
Customers: delays, broken promises, may go elsewhere
Business: lost money, overtime, poor reputation
Good attendance builds trust or chances of promotion

practical1.title: Write a workshop code of conduct and solve ethics case cards
practical1.brief: As a group, write a code of conduct for one work area at the Centre, such as the welding shop, the salon or the electrical lab, and then decide what a professional would do in a set of real-life cases. Part 1: agree and write at least 10 clear rules, covering punctuality, dress and PPE, honesty, confidentiality, use of tools and materials, phones, respect, safety and reporting problems. Each member writes at least two of the rules on the final poster. Part 2: the assessor gives the group one case card per member, for example a customer who overpays, a supplier who offers a gift, a co-worker who asks you to sign in for them, or a neighbour who wants a job done for cash with the Centre's materials. Each member leads the group discussion on one card and writes the group's answer on a case sheet: what to do, and why. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical.
materials: Chart paper and markers for the code of conduct poster
Case cards from the assessor (one per member)
Masking tape or pins to put the poster up
photos: The group planning the code of conduct, with the notes visible
The finished code of conduct poster, clear enough to read
Each member leading the discussion of a case card (one photo per member)
The poster put up in the work area it was written for
checklist: Suggested at least two clear, sensible rules for the code of conduct
Wrote their rules neatly and correctly on the poster
Led the discussion of a case card and let others speak
Gave an answer to the case that is honest, legal and safe
Explained the reason for the answer in their own words
Listened to and respected other members' views
Did a fair share of the group's work
safety: Use markers in a ventilated room and put the caps back on
Put the poster up from the floor or a stable step only if the assessor allows; do not stand on chairs
Keep bags, chart paper and cables out of walkways

practical2.title: Role play: handling a customer's job professionally from start to finish
practical2.brief: As a group, act out one customer's job from first visit to final complaint, showing professional and ethical behaviour at each stage. The job can be from any trade, for example a grill for a front door, a set of salon treatments, or a new socket outlet. Before starting, each member checks their own appearance against a simple dress and hygiene checklist and the group photographs it. Then share the stages so that each member leads one: greeting the customer and finding out what they want; giving an honest written quotation; telling the customer about a delay and giving a new date; refusing a gift or a cash "side deal" politely; and dealing calmly with a complaint at the end. Another member plays the customer for each stage. The rest observe and note good practice on an observation sheet. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in the quotation, the job card and the observation sheets once for the whole group.
materials: Dress and hygiene checklist (one per member)
Blank quotation form and job card
Customer role cards from the assessor
A table and chairs set up as a reception area
photos: Each member in clean uniform or work clothes, with their completed dress and hygiene checklist
The greeting stage of the role play
The completed written quotation and job card
The member refusing a gift or side deal politely
The complaint stage, and the completed observation sheets
checklist: Arrived on time and was dressed cleanly and correctly for the trade
Greeted the customer politely and listened to what they wanted
Gave honest, clear information about price and time
Told the customer about the delay early and gave a new date
Refused the gift or side deal politely and gave a reason
Stayed calm and professional when dealing with the complaint
Kept the customer's details private and recorded them only on the job card
safety: Keep the role play calm: no shouting, pushing or touching
Keep a clear path to the exit, with no trailing cables
Use made-up names, numbers and prices; no real customer details
